title: Regional PPK Risk-Adjusted Allocator (working sheet)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet is a compact, scenario-driven spreadsheet to allocate token PPK (price-per-thousand tokens) capacity across regions and model families while explicitly accounting for short-term supply risk (spot GPU variability), latency SLO tiers, and cache/batching leverage. The goal is to produce an operational allocation matrix that can be used by the routing layer and finance to set per-region price bands and reserve sizing.
body_2:
Layout and key tabs (described as text for Drive representation):
- Inputs: regional traffic share, historical region spot volatility (weekly std dev), average sequence length distribution per workload, baseline model PPK (unquantized), quantized model PPK delta, cache hit rate baseline, batching efficiency factor per latency tier. Cells referenced as examples: Inputs!B3:B10 (regions), Inputs!C3:C10 (traffic %), Inputs!D3:D10 (spot volatility pct), Inputs!E3:E10 (avg seq len).
- Scenario assumptions: rows for Conservative / Base / Aggressive with multipliers applied to spot volatility and demand tail. Example cells: Scenarios!B2 (Conservative multiplier = 1.25), Scenarios!B3 (Base = 1.0), Scenarios!B4 (Aggressive = 0.8).
- Cost model: per-region computed COGS per 1k tokens combining GPU amortization, power, license, and network egress. Formula examples: CostModel!F = (GpuHourlyAmort * UtilizationAdj + LicenseAmort/slots + PowerPerHour/slots) / (TokensPerHour/1000).
- PPK risk adjuster: for each region and scenario compute RiskAdjPPK = BaselinePPK * (1 + SpotVolatility*VolSensitivity) * DemandTailFactor - CacheSavings. See cells: RiskAdj!C3 = =Inputs!G3*(1+Inputs!D3*Scenarios!B2) - Inputs!H3.
- Allocator: produces per-region suggested price floor, target PPK, and emergency fallback PPK (quantized/fallback model). Example output columns: Region, TargetPPK, EmergencyPPK, TargetMarginPct, ReservedSlots, CanaryReservePct.
- Sensitivities: small Monte Carlo sampler tab (1000 iterations) that perturbs region volatility and demand spikes to estimate 95th percentile PPK and required reserved capacity. Not full Monte Carlo here, just lightweight sampling for quick checks.

Highlights of the calculation approach (unique decisions):
1) Volatility-weighted hedging: instead of a flat uplift, each region gets a volatility multiplier tied to measured weekly spot standard deviation. Regions with >15% spot SD get an additional buffer multiplier. This creates a smoothly varying reserve rather than tiered bands.
2) Latency-aware batching credit: for latency SLO <150ms we apply a reduced batching efficiency (0.6x) vs background batchable workloads (1.25x). The allocator splits workloads into latency buckets and computes blended tokens-per-hour.
3) Cache-first token subtraction: token-level cache savings are subtracted before margin calculation (cache assumed to reduce billable tokens; cell Inputs!H = estimated cache hit tokens per request).
4) Quantized emergency fallback: EmergencyPPK uses a quantized model PPK at 40% lower compute cost but with an estimated quality delta penalty encoded as a 'quality tax' (applied to margin targets rather than price).
5) Canary reserve: recommended 2-8% of reserved slots per region that must be kept cold for canary rollouts and fallbacks; percent scales with region volatility.
body_3:
Representative small table (textualized) from Allocator tab showing Base scenario outputs:
- us-west-2 | traffic 28% | BaselinePPK $0.032 | TargetPPK $0.039 | EmergencyPPK $0.020 | TargetMargin 63% | ReservedSlots 46
- eu-west-1 | traffic 18% | BaselinePPK $0.036 | TargetPPK $0.045 | EmergencyPPK $0.022 | TargetMargin 60% | ReservedSlots 34
- ap-south-1 | traffic 6% | BaselinePPK $0.047 | TargetPPK $0.058 | EmergencyPPK $0.027 | TargetMargin 55% | ReservedSlots 8
Numbers above are illustrative outputs (not final), produced by combining local cost, volatility uplift (Base scenario), and latency/batching mix.

Key formulas called out for reviewers (verbatim):
- TokensPerHour = Slots * SeqPerRequest * ReqPerSlotPerHour * BatchingFactor
- CostPer1k = (HourlyGpuAmort*UtilAdj + HourlyPower + LicenseHourly)/ (TokensPerHour/1000)
- RiskAdjPPK = CostPer1k * (1 + SpotSD*VolSensitivity) / (1 - DesiredMargin)
- EmergencyPPK = QuantizedCostPer1k * (1 + QualityTax)
Where VolSensitivity is tunable (default 0.6), QualityTax default = 0.12 (applied to margin target).

Operational recommendations and actionables (short, prioritized):
1) Run the sheet against last 90 days of region spot prices and update Inputs!D values. Target date: 10/18/2025. Owner: Liam Chen.
2) Integrate Allocator outputs into routing-policy config draft (route weights + fallback thresholds). Small PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/142. Owner: Marcel DuPont.
3) Finance review: validate license and amort numbers (Inputs!K-L). If license amort per GPU changes >5%, re-run sensitivity. Owner: Aisha Khan.
4) Canary playbook: define activation rules for EmergencyPPK fallback and canary reserve drain. Draft a one-pager and link to rollout runbook.
5) Short-term experiment: region us-west-2 can increase reserve by 10 slots for 72 hours during scheduled AI holiday traffic to validate model. If realized PPK > 110% of TargetPPK, trigger emergency fallback.

Open questions / TODOs left in-sheet (notes to self style):
- Should VolSensitivity be set as a function of observed demand correlation across regions (currently static 0.6)?
- Need to formalize how quality tax maps to contract SLAs for enterprise customers (per-customer exemptions?).
- Add an automated import from CostCenter daily spot report (CSV) to keep volatility up-to-date.

Appendix: quick provenance and assumptions (short):
- Cost assumptions use internal amort tables as of 2025-08; power and license amort are blended by region.
- Cache hit and batching efficiencies are based on telemetry samples from July–August 2025 across 12 workloads.
- This sheet is intentionally compact: full model with full Monte Carlo lives in optimize/ppk-montecarlo-master (linked PR above).

Next steps for the draft: convert the key outputs (Region, TargetPPK, EmergencyPPK, ReservedSlots) into a small CSV export that the routing config generator can consume. Also add an example fallback policy JSON snippet in a notes tab.
